Even as many women, including some on the left, have begun moving away from hook-up culture, @alexandracooper has remained adamantly for it, notes @AshMcG

While we congratulate her on her pregnancy news, we should be concerned about the effects of her misleading dating and relationship advice on countless young women.

More here: ifstudies.org/blog/alex-coop…

Stop being so weird about Alex Cooper, whose choices -- go to college, work, date, marry, procreate -- are totally normal. 
newstatesman.com/world/ameri…
"omg you people can't do anything" turning out to be the most evergreen tweet of all time
If you have the capacity to engage in a days-long twitter fight about DoorDash you probably have the capacity to make yourself something to eat.

The real move is to fly first class but register your children in coach as unaccompanied minors so you don't even have to deal with getting them to baggage claim.


New York Post (@nypost)

Nick Lachey claims ex Jessica Simpson flew in first class while her 3 kids sat in economy during 6-hour flight trib.al/KcV5hzC





— https://nitter.net/nypost/status/2055674277018452030#m

My other hot take is that this all costs significantly more than making your own sandwich AND it is really bad for you! Like good lord no one needs to eat a quarter pound chopped brisket sandwich with large curly fries and a large diet coke for a normal weekday lunch??


The Refined Populist (@RefinedPopulist)

A large, fast food value meal costs ~$20 with tax. What are they supposed to do?











— https://nitter.net/RefinedPopulist/status/2056728976891019325#m

I need to sign off of this discourse but like... a bag of Whole Foods bread is $4.50. A block of cheddar is $2.99. A half-pound of sliced deli turkey is $7. A container of mustard is $3. That adds up to less than $20. 

Can you even get a sandwich delivered via DoorDash for less than $20?

New contender for the worst contribution to the DoorDash discourse: Young people are ordering DoorDash because they can't afford concerts and there is literally nothing else for them to do. Like say... cook.

Every aspect of this debate is making me want to hurl myself off a cliff. No, you do not need to eat PB&J and chips for lunch every single day to save money. There is in fact an enormous universe of food that is simple to prepare, healthier than DoorDash, and way more affordable than DoorDash.

Chickpeas sauteed with onion and garlic and tossed with pasta. Chickpeas sauteed with onion and garlic and shrimp. Chickpeas sauteed with onion and garlic and *tomatoes* and tossed with pasta. Chickpeas sauteed with onion and garlic and *tomatoes* and shrimp. Still love 'em.

One summer I subletted a room from a friend and I ate chickpeas for so many dinners she asked if I had an eating disorder 😂


Matthew Yglesias (@mattyglesias)

There are lots of perfectly good reasons to order DoorDash rather than be maximally thrifty, but people should know the option to spend less money is very much available. Eat an apple. Keep some tuna in your pantry. 

slowboring.com/p/doordash-an…





— https://nitter.net/mattyglesias/status/2057267607175152080#m

The problems are not with the college-educated Millennial girlbosses and Alex Coopers of the world. Those women are as likely to get married now as women born in 1940 were. Marriage declines are most pronounced among non-college women. So instead of screaming at the pregnant 31-year-old successful college grad, maybe give a helping hand to women who are struggling? 
 
Full piece here: throughline.news/p/what-if-t…

Teen births are way down. Unintended pregnancy rates have also dropped substantially, especially among teenagers and women in their early 20s. By contrast, intended pregnancies among women in their late 30s and 40s have jumped to record highs. More women are using contraception, so they’re having children when they want them. More women are delaying having children because more of them are finishing high school, going to college, and working for pay. They can afford to be pickier about partners,

Instead of fighting back against Big Food and some of the worst befoulers of our food, water, and environment, the Trump administration has elevated them and done their bidding.

(in other words, the winning continues 😡)

@jillfilipovic.bsky.social's latest:

open.substack.com/pub/jill/p/i...

"The resentment directed towards Cooper isn’t because she sold one version of womanhood while living another; it’s because she lived the kind of autonomous life feminists fought for, and it’s going great"

Very much enjoyed this by @jillfilipovic.bsky.social

www.newstatesman.com/world/americ...
Along with @jillfilipovic.bsky.social, I was on the @thebrianlehrershow.bsky.social this morning to help interpret US birth rates and discuss current efforts to raise them. wnyc.org/browse/shows...

The most important piece I've read this year, up with similarly important works by @jillfilipovic.bsky.social, @pennyred.bsky.social, and Dale Beran analyzing different aspects of this same culture shift.

Women are not protected: not by living in liberal states, not by having the money to cross state lines, and, given the impact of abortion bans on women who are miscarrying, not even by not having elective abortions.

We were told that Roe fueled the culture wars and that returning the abortion question to the states would bring reasoned debate, a democratic process, and then stability. Instead the anti-abortion movement has created nothing but chaos and confusion.
slate.com/news-and-pol...

In @nytopinion.nytimes.com

Friday’s federal appeals decision on the abortion pill mifepristone sends a clear message, Jill Filipovic writes in a guest essay: “No woman in America, no matter where she lives, has total control over whether to continue or end a pregnancy.”

Yes, @jillfilipovic.bsky.social appropriately sums up the current Fed Soc "conservative" Supreme Court. Note, they are just radical and extremist, what they are has nothing whatsoever to do with "conservatism".
www.nytimes.com/2026/05/02/o...
i was told by john roberts and sam alito that racism is over so i won't worry about white republicans in the south jumping over themselves to end black political representation wherever they can

Marking our 250th year by having the British King visit to remind us about the development of the rule of law, while the president reads lines presumably written by Stephen Miller about the transcendent nobility of the mythic English blood.
Call me when the NYT is ready for a "12 Bitches Who Were Right about Everything" piece.

I truly think we've made something special. So if this sounds like something you might like, I hope you take the leap and sign up. Full disclosure it's mostly women. Most come alone, some bring a friend. But you can come as you are, whoever you are, with whoever you want to come with.

Retreats are very very very fun and I hope you'll consider joining me! Not to toot my own horn too loudly but ever since my collaborator Emily and I hosted our first retreat together we've had multiple repeat retreaters return on every single retreat, and at this point we've done at least a dozen.

Imagine taking a week to have all of your needs met: someone offering you creative practice, someone offering you movement practice, dinner reservations made, interesting people around the table, wine poured on when you arrive. Space to make and move and be. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

I host writing and yoga retreats around the world. And no, "go on a yoga retreat" is not the answer to society-wide loneliness or burnout or any Big Huge Problems. But it is one way to give yourself a damn break. To have fun. To exhale. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece
